class Conversation < ApplicationRecord
  include Diaspora::Federated::Base
  include Diaspora::Fields::Guid
  include Diaspora::Fields::Author

  has_many :conversation_visibilities, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :participants, class_name: "Person", through: :conversation_visibilities, source: :person
  has_many :messages, -> { order("created_at ASC") }, inverse_of: :conversation

  validate :local_recipients

  def local_recipients
    recipients.each do |recipient|
      if recipient.local?
        unless recipient.owner.contacts.where(person_id: author.id).any? ||
            (author.owner && author.owner.podmin_account?)
          errors.add(:all_recipients, "recipient not allowed")
        end
      end
    end
  end

  accepts_nested_attributes_for :messages

  def recipients
    self.participants - [self.author]
  end

  def first_unread_message(user)
    if visibility = self.conversation_visibilities.where(:person_id => user.person.id).where('unread > 0').first

    end
  end

  def set_read(user)
    visibility = conversation_visibilities.find_by(person_id: user.person.id)

    visibility.unread = 0

I submitted two review items in `out/review_items.json` (marker `review_items.submitted`, digest checked). The more serious one shows that the policy is missing a database write this endpoint can make.

**1. Not the same read: a missing write** (`catchable: true`). The mock that stands in for `destroy` in the shared targets file (`targets/core.rb` ~L1539) replaces Rails' whole `destroy` method, so model callbacks never run. `ConversationVisibility` has an `after_destroy :check_orphan_conversation` callback that the corpus never sees.

I ran a measurement in `batch/measure_destroy.rb`: real ActiveRecord, no mocks, on a private copy of the sqlite database. It replays the controller's data access at model level; it is not a full HTTP request. Calling `vis.destroy` issues, after the recorded `DELETE`:
- **Always:** a read of the conversation by id and a participant `COUNT(*)`. The policy already allows both shapes, so their absence lets nothing extra through.
- **When the user was the conversation's last participant:** a read of the conversation's visibility rows, then `DELETE FROM "conversations" WHERE "conversations"."id" = ?`.

No rule in the policy allows that delete, and the condition that triggers it was never explored. On the production MySQL schema, a foreign key (`db/schema.rb:632`) would also delete the conversation's messages. I took that from the schema and didn't measure it, because sqlite doesn't enforce the key.

I proposed, but did not apply, two real-mode test scenarios: one where the user is the last participant and one with two participants. Either recording would make the existing shape check flag this automatically. That only works once someone builds the code that drives real-mode requests, which doesn't exist yet.

**2. Same read** (`catchable: true`). The lookup `.where(person_id:, conversation_id:).first` really runs with `ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT ?`; the recorded statement has neither. The two columns form a unique index (`db/schema.rb:146`), so at most one row can match and ordering or limiting changes nothing. That reasoning comes from the schema; I didn't run anything that tried to disprove it. The item states what would disprove it: a deployed database without that index, or a recording where this lookup returns more than one row.

**Escalation:** fixing the corpus itself means changing the shared targets file, which affects every endpoint whose saved or destroyed model has callbacks. I'm not allowed to make that change, so I filed `ctl/ask/destroy-mock-skips-after-destroy-callbacks.json` (class `shared`). No answer had arrived by submission, and item 1 says so.

I made no other claims. The users, people and profiles reads probably differ only by `LIMIT`/`ORDER`, but I didn't measure them.
